metadata.title: A quantitative spectral analysis of 14 hypervelocity stars from the MMT survey

evidence.quote: We reanalyzed low-resolution optical spectra of 14 HVSs from the MMT HVS survey

The MMT HVS survey by Brown et al. (2014) discovered 38
late B-type HVSs, 16 of which are considered to be bound to the
Galaxy. We selected the 14 most interesting ones, that is, those
stars which have proper motions measured by HST.

notes: HVS 1 (SDSS J090744.99+024506.9), HVS 4 (SDSS J091301.01+305119.8), HVS 5 (SDSS J091759.48+672238.3), HVS 6 (SDSS J110557.45+093439.5), HVS 7 (SDSS J113312.12+010824.9), HVS 8 (SDSS J094214.04+200322.1), HVS 9 (SDSS J102137.08-005234.8), HVS 10 (SDSS J120337.85+180250.4), HVS 12 (SDSS J105009.60+031550.7), HVS 13 (SDSS J105248.31-000133.9), B434 (SDSS J110224.37+025002.8), B485 (SDSS J101018.82+302028.1), B711 (SDSS J142001.94+124404.8), and B733 (SDSS J144955.58+310351.4): the paper describes them as the 14 HVSs from the Brown et al. (2014) MMT HVS survey and reanalyzes their spectra (T:p1-b8, T:p1-b16). This is treated as follow-up of previously identified HVS candidates. The paper does not make an individual present-day Galactic-boundness determination; because it also states that 16 of the 38 survey HVSs are considered bound without mapping them (T:p1-b16), the blanket HVS label alone is not treated here as a new unbound finding. Table 1 pairs each HVS/B name with its SDSS identifier (T:p5-b0; I:p5-b0). B711 remains in the sample although reclassified as an A-type star (T:p2-b8).

HVS 1: At T:p5-b0, Table 1 reports HVS 1 (SDSS J090744.99+024506.9) with radial velocity and distance but no explicit equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motions, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probabilities. The SDSS designation was not treated as an explicit astrometric measurement because parsing/converting it would add values not directly reported as quantities. The table gives both asymmetric distance uncertainties and a separate final 1σ distance uncertainty; both are recorded.

HVS 4: For HVS 4, no right ascension, declination, parallax, proper-motion components, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported. The SDSS designation contains coordinate-like fields, but no equatorial coordinate values are tabulated; these were not converted. Table 1 lists the distance once with 99%-confidence error ranges and also provides a separate 1σ distance error column; both are recorded. Locations: T:p5-b0 and I:p5-b0.

HVS 5: The position is taken from the SDSS J designation in T:p5-b0; the paper does not provide a separate RA/Dec table. In T:p5-b0, HVS 5's distance is 31.2 kpc with two uncertainty representations: the first error pair (+8.3/−6.4 kpc) is the 99%-confidence limit, while the second (+3.2/−2.5 kpc) corresponds to the 1σ uncertainty. No individual parallax, proper motions, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS 5.

HVS 6: Target HVS 6 is identified as SDSS J110557.45+093439.5. Its RA and Dec are taken from the SDSS designation in Table 1, since no separate coordinate columns are given. For distance, Table 1 reports 57.7 kpc with a 99%-confidence range +17.1/-18.5 kpc and a separate 1σ range +6.6/-7.2 kpc; both uncertainty conventions are recorded. The radial-velocity reference frame is not explicitly specified in the supplied text.

HVS 7: Coordinates are not given in a separate astrometric column; they are taken from the SDSS J2000 designation for HVS 7 in Table 1 (T:p5-b0/I:p5-b0). For the distance, the tabulated 1σ uncertainty is used in the error fields; the same table entry also gives 99%-confidence limits of +11.1/-9.5 kpc. No individual parallax, proper motion, Galactic-rest-frame velocity, Galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is tabulated for this star.

HVS 8: For HVS 8 = SDSS J094214.04+200322.1, no individual parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported. RA/Dec are taken from the J2000 SDSS designation because no separate coordinate columns are given. Table 1 lists the distance as 37.2 kpc with +11.4/-9.2 (99% confidence limits) and separately gives a 1σ column of +4.4/-3.6; both distance uncertainty representations are retained (T:p5-b0, I:p5-b0).

HVS 9: HVS 9 corresponds to SDSS J102137.08-005234.8 in Table 1 (T:p5-b0). Both the 99%-confidence-limit distance uncertainty (+16.0/-17.8 kpc) and the separate 1σ uncertainty (+6.2/-7.0 kpc) are retained; the latter is obtained by dividing the former by 2.576 per the table notes. No separate right ascension, declination, parallax, proper-motion, Galactocentric-radius, rest-frame-speed, or bound-probability values are tabulated for HVS 9.

HVS 10: Target is HVS 10 (SDSS J120337.85+180250.4), the corresponding row of Table 1 (T:p5-b0). The paper reports this star's radial velocity and spectroscopic distance. It does not report equatorial coordinates as tabulated quantities, parallax, proper motions, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS 10. The distance column lists 99%-confidence asymmetric uncertainties, and the adjacent 1σ column gives the corresponding 1σ distance uncertainties; both are recorded without conversion.

HVS 12: Target HVS 12 corresponds to SDSS J105009.60+031550.7 (T:p5-b0/I:p5-b0). Table 1 reports two distance-uncertainty representations for HVS 12: +23.1/-15.8 kpc in the d column and +9.0/-6.1 kpc in the separate 1σ column; both are retained. The paper does not tabulate separate right ascension/declination, parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for this star.

HVS 13: For HVS 13 (= SDSS J105248.31-000133.9), the target-list quantities reported per star are the Table 1 spectroscopic distance and radial velocity. The distance is recorded with both the table's 99%-confidence errors and its comparison 1σ errors; the table note states that the 1σ limits are obtained by dividing the 99%-confidence limits by 2.576. No individual parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported. The RA/Dec embedded in the SDSS designation were not treated as independent coordinate measurements.

B434: Values are from Table 1 for B434. The paper does not tabulate independent astrometric coordinates; the RA and Dec given here are those encoded in the SDSS designation. Table 1 lists distance uncertainties at 99% confidence and also gives separate 1σ distance uncertainties obtained by dividing the 99% confidence limits by 2.576.

B485: B485 is matched to SDSS J101018.82+302028.1 in Table 1 (T:p5-b0/I:p5-b0). Table 1 reports the distance with both 99%-confidence limits (d column) and a separate 1σ column; both are retained. No individual parallax, proper motion, RA/Dec, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star in the supplied material.

B711: Table 1 reports B711's distance as 28.5 kpc with 99%-confidence asymmetric errors +8.0/-5.5 and a separate 1σ column +3.1/-2.2; both are retained. Coordinates are not tabulated in separate RA/Dec columns but are encoded in the SDSS object designation in Table 1 (T:p5-b0, I:p5-b0). The abstract (T:p1-b9) gives a 30-100 kpc distance range, whereas Sect. 5 (T:p3-b7) states 10-100 kpc and Table 1 contains B711 at 28.5 kpc; this does not alter the individual tabulated value.

B733: Table 1 (T:p5-b0; I:p5-b0) reports B733's distance as 9.9 kpc with asymmetric 99% confidence limits (+1.7/-2.1 kpc) and a corresponding 1σ uncertainty range (+0.7/-0.9 kpc); both reported error conventions are retained. No explicit equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motions, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability are reported for B733.
